newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Alcoa in pact to sell alumina to China.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Alcoa in pact to sell alumina to China.

text.p: Alcoa World Alumina and Chemicals said on Tuesday it has reached an agreement to sell alumina to China.
The agreement was reached with Sino Mining Ltd, wholly-owned by China National Nonferrous Metal Industry Corp (CNNC), for the purchase of alumina for the CNNC smelter system.
The arrangement entitles a subsidiary of Sino Mining to take 400,000 tonnes of alumina a year for 30 years, with an option to increase its tonnage if it requires more alumina.
Alcoa World Alumina is 60 percent owned by Aluminum Co of America and 40 percent by WMC Ltd.
Sino Mining would make an advance lump-sum payment of $240 million to Alocoa World Alumina related to the 400,000-tonne sales agreement, the company said.

Robert Slagle, president of Alcoa World Alumina, said in a statement the agreement represented an important step in growing the company's global business, while confirming a commitment to the chinese alumina market.
Nicholas Curtis, president and chief executive officer of Sino Mining, said in a statement the transaction would reduce China's dependence spot market purchases of alumina.
China has been a major importer of spot alumina for some time. he said.
Analysts expect China to produce in excess of one million tonnes of aluminium annually for the next several years, with that figure growing in step with industrial growth.
CNNC alone is estimated by Alcoa World Alumina to smelt over 735,000 tonnes of aluminium a year.
Generally, it takes two tonnes of alumina to produce one tonne of aluminium.
Australia is a main world supplier of alumina.

In 1996/97, it is forecast to produce 13.3 million tonnes of alumina against world prodcution of 45.5 million tonnes in calendar 1996, the Australian Bureau of Agriculture and Research Economics (ABARE) said in a recent report.
